rules.sentence: A full body skin examination should be performed, including careful evaluation of the mucous membranes and the nails for other signs of psoriasis and to exclude other causes of pustulosis.
Pustular psoriasis can be diffuse or localized.
Pustular psoriasis appears as numerous discrete or confluent superficial, yellowish pustules on a background of erythema.

Studies have also identified an IL-36 receptor antagonist deficiency in patients with pustular psoriasis, and these patients have been successfully treated with a novel monoclonal antibody against the IL-36 receptor.[8]
